main_task: Pre-approve the app “Google Calendar” for workspace members
main_steps: Click Admin in the left sidebar.
Click Apps and workflows in the menu that appears.
Click Browse in the top-right corner of the Slack Marketplace window.
Click the search field at the top, type Google Calendar, and press Enter.
Click the Google Calendar app in the search results.
On the app page, click the Approve button.
In the confirmation dialog, click Approve to finish.

main_task: Create a personal reminder that will notify you in 5 minutes
main_steps: Click the message field at the bottom of the currently open channel.
Type "/remind me \"Review project plan\" in 5 minutes" (without the outer quotes).
Press Enter.

main_task: Configure Slack to send notifications only on weekdays from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM
main_steps: Click your profile picture in the Slack sidebar.
Click Preferences in the menu that appears.
Scroll to the Notification schedule section.
Click the Allow notifications drop-down list.
Select Weekdays.
Click the Start time field and choose 9:00 AM.
Click the End time field and choose 5:00 PM.
Click the close icon at the top-right of the Preferences window.

setup_task: (Setup) Start a Huddle in the #general channel
setup_steps: Click the “#general” channel in the left sidebar.
Click the headphones “Start a huddle” icon in the channel header.
Click the “Start huddle” button in the dialog.
main_task: Open the Huddle canvas for taking meeting notes
main_steps: Locate the huddle controls at the bottom right of the huddle window.
Click the canvas icon (a square with a pencil) to open the notes canvas.

main_task: Create a custom view that shows only unread mentions and threads from the #general channel
main_steps: Click Activity in the left sidebar.
Click the plus (+) icon at the top of the Activity pane.
Click Create a custom view.
In the Title field, type Important Unreads.
Click the radio button for Detailed layout.
Click the Only show unreads toggle so it is on.
Check the box next to Mentions & reactions.
Check the box next to Threads.
Click the Select channels or sections drop-down.
Click #general in the list.
Click Save.

main_task: Display the Channels analytics for the last 30 days
main_steps: Click the organization name in the Slack sidebar.
Click Tools & settings in the menu.
Click Workspace analytics.
Click the Channels tab at the top of the analytics window.
Click the date range button that shows Last 28 days.
Select Last 30 days from the drop-down list.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a private channel that will later be converted to public
setup_steps: Click the   +   button next to Channels in the left sidebar.
Select Create a channel.
In the Channel name field, type test-private.
Turn on the Make private toggle so it is enabled.
Click Create.
Click Skip for now if invited members are requested.
main_task: Convert the “test-private” channel from private to public
main_steps: Click the test-private channel in the left sidebar.
Click the channel name test-private at the top of the conversation header.
Click the Settings tab in the channel details window.
Scroll (if necessary) and click Change to a public channel.
In the confirmation dialog, click Convert to Public.

main_task: Remove the “#general” channel from the list of default channels
main_steps: Click the workspace name at the top of the left sidebar.
Click Tools & settings.
Click Workspace settings.
Next to Default Channels, click Expand.
Click the small white x to the right of “#general”.
Click Save.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a sample automation rule named “Temp Rule”
setup_steps: Click Admin in the left sidebar.
Click Apps and workflows from the menu.
In the Slack Marketplace window, click Requests in the left sidebar.
Click Automation rules.
Click Create rule.
In the Rule name field, type Temp Rule.
Click Save.
Click Done to finish creating the rule.
main_task: Remove the “Temp Rule” automation rule
main_steps: Click Admin in the left sidebar.
Click Apps and workflows.
In the Slack Marketplace window, click Requests in the left sidebar.
Click Automation rules to view the list of rules.
Click the three dots icon next to the Temp Rule.
Click Remove.
In the confirmation dialog, click Remove to confirm.

setup_task: (Setup) Generate a Slack Connect direct message invitation that appears in your primary workspace
setup_steps: Click the workspace name in the top-left corner of Slack.
Click Sign in to another workspace.
Enter the sign-in details for a second workspace you have access to and click Continue.
In the second workspace, click the plus (+) icon next to Direct Messages in the sidebar.
Click Slack Connect.
In the email field, type the email address that belongs to your primary workspace and press Enter.
Click Invite.
Click Done to finish sending the invitation.
Click the workspace switcher in the top-left corner and select your primary workspace to return to it.
Wait a moment until the Slack Connect invitation banner appears or refresh the Home view if necessary.
main_task: Block all future Slack Connect invitations from the sender of the newly received invitation
main_steps: Click Home in the sidebar to make sure you are on the workspace’s home screen.
Click Directories near the top of the page.
Click the External tab at the top of the Directories page.
Find the pending invitation in the list and click Ignore to the right of it.
In the dialog that opens, click Block invitations from this person.
Click Block Invitations to confirm.

setup_task: (Setup) Open the #general channel so its conversation header is visible
setup_steps: In the left sidebar, click Channels to expand the list if it is collapsed.
Click the channel named #general.
main_task: Hide the “Files” tab from the #general channel header
main_steps: Click the plus (+) icon at the right end of the header tabs row.
Click Edit tabs.
Hover the mouse pointer over the tab labeled Files in the list that appears.
Click the eye icon beside Files to hide the tab.
Click Done.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a canvas called “Q1 Goals” inside the #general channel
setup_steps: Click the “#general” channel in the left sidebar.
Click the plus (+) button to the left of the message field.
In the menu that appears, click “Canvas”.
In the Title field, type Q1 Goals.
Click the Create button.
Click the Close (×) button in the upper-right corner of the canvas window to return to the channel view.
main_task: Add a new tab named “Goals” that features the “Q1 Goals” canvas
main_steps: In the channel header, click the + (Add a tab) button to the right of the existing tabs.
Click “Canvas or list”.
Click the radio button next to the canvas titled Q1 Goals.
Click Next.
In the Tab name box, type Goals.
Click Add.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a sample icon file for upload
setup_steps: Press the Windows key.
Type Paint and press Enter.
Click the rectangle tool in the toolbar.
Drag on the blank canvas to draw a small square.
Press Ctrl+S.
In the Save As dialog, click Desktop in the left pane.
In the File name box, type OrgIcon.png.
Click the Save button.
Click the Close button to exit Paint.
main_task: Upload the created “OrgIcon.png” as the organization icon
main_steps: In Slack, click your organization name at the top of the left sidebar.
Click Tools & settings in the menu that appears.
Click Customize in the submenu.
In the left sidebar of the Customize window, click Settings.
Click Organization Info.
Next to the Details section, click Edit.
Under Icon, click Choose File.
In the file dialog, click Desktop.
Double-click OrgIcon.png.
Click Save.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a folder named “Drafts” in the #general channel
setup_steps: Click the #general channel in the left sidebar to open it.
At the top of the conversation, click the + icon labeled “Add bookmark”.
Click New folder.
Type Drafts.
Press Enter.
main_task: Rename the “Drafts” folder to “Final Drafts”
main_steps: In the bookmarks bar, click the folder named Drafts to open it.
Click the three dots icon in the top-right corner of the folder view.
Click Rename folder.
Type Final Drafts.
Press Enter.

main_task: Revoke the first pending external invitation
main_steps: Click Directories in the left-hand sidebar on the Home screen.
Click External at the top of the Directory page.
Click View invitations.
Hover the mouse pointer over the first invitation in the list.
Click the revoke icon that appears on the right of that invitation row.
In the confirmation dialog, click Revoke.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a new channel that you manage
setup_steps: Click the “+” button next to “Channels” in the left sidebar.
Click “Create a channel”.
Type “demo-permissions” in the Channel Name field.
Click “Create”.
Click “Skip for now” if invited members are prompted.
main_task: Restrict tab editing to only Channel Managers in the “demo-permissions” channel
main_steps: Click “demo-permissions” in the left sidebar to open the channel.
Click the channel name “demo-permissions” at the top of the conversation header.
Click “Settings”.
Click the drop-down menu below “Choose who can add, remove, and reorder tabs”.
Select “Only Channel Managers”.
Click the “✕” close icon in the upper-right of the dialog.

main_task: Open the list of blocked Slack Connect invitations
main_steps: Click your profile picture in the left sidebar.
Click Preferences in the menu that appears.
In the Preferences window, click Privacy & visibility in the left pane.
Scroll to the section labeled Invitations you’ve blocked.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a new public channel named “team-huddle” that includes you and “Alex”
setup_steps: Click the “+” button next to “Channels” in the left sidebar.
Click “Create a channel”.
In the “Name” field, type team-huddle.
Click “Create”.
In the “Add people” field, type Alex.
Click Alex in the dropdown list.
Click “Add”.
Click “Done”.
main_task: Start a huddle in the channel and invite Alex to it
main_steps: Click the channel team-huddle in the left sidebar.
In the channel header, click the headphones icon labeled “Start a huddle”.
Click the person-plus (Add people) button in the huddle controls bar.
Type Alex in the search box.
Click Alex in the list.
Click “Invite”.

main_task: Record a video clip in the #general channel with background blur enabled and send it with a generated transcript
main_steps: Click the #general channel in the sidebar.
Click the message field at the bottom.
Click the plus (+) icon next to the message field.
Click "Record a video clip" in the menu.
In the recording window, click the Blur background button to enable it.
Click the Record button to start recording.
Click the Record button again to stop recording.
Click Use Video.
Click Generate transcript below the clip preview.
Click the paper plane icon to send the clip.

main_task: Hide the “Phone number” profile field and publish the change
main_steps: Click the workspace name at the top of the left sidebar.
Hover over Tools & settings.
Click Workspace settings.
Click Menu at the top of the settings page.
Click Profiles in the left sidebar.
Locate the “Phone number” field in the list of profile fields.
Click the toggle next to “Phone number” to switch it off.
Click Publish Changes in the upper-right corner.

setup_task: (Setup) Join a Salesforce channel and create a custom section to move it into
setup_steps: Click the “+” button next to Channels in the left sidebar.
Type “acme-corp” in the search field.
Click the result named “acme-corp” that displays the Salesforce cloud icon.
Click the Join button to join the channel.
Scroll to the bottom of the channel list in the sidebar and click Add section.
Type “Key Accounts” in the section name field.
Press Enter to create the new custom section.
main_task: Move the “acme-corp” Salesforce channel from the Salesforce channels section to the “Key Accounts” custom section
main_steps: Locate the “acme-corp” channel under the Salesforce channels section in the sidebar.
Click and hold the “acme-corp” channel name.
Drag the channel into the “Key Accounts” section until the section highlights.
Release the mouse button to drop the channel into the section.

main_task: Notify all members in the #general channel about an emergency drill using @everyone
main_steps: Click the “general” channel in the left sidebar.
Click the message input field at the bottom of the channel.
Type "@everyone Please note that there will be an emergency evacuation drill at 3 PM."
Press Enter.

main_task: Accept a pending external invitation
main_steps: Click Home in the left sidebar.
Click Directories near the top of the Home view.
Click External at the top of the Directories page.
Click Accept to the right of the pending invitation entry.
Review the invitation details.
Click Accept Invitation.

main_task: Send a message that notifies only currently active members using @here
main_steps: Click the channel named “general” in the left sidebar.
Click into the message input box at the bottom.
Type “@here Lunch in 5 minutes.”
Press Enter.

setup_task: (Setup) Post a sample message to react to
setup_steps: Click the message input field at the bottom of the #general channel.
Type "Sample message for emoji reaction".
Press Enter.
main_task: Add a 👍 (thumbs up) emoji reaction to the posted message
main_steps: Hover the cursor over the "Sample message for emoji reaction" message until the action icons appear.
Click the Add reaction (smiley face with a plus) icon.
Type "thumbsup" in the emoji search field.
Click the 👍 emoji from the search results.

setup_task: (Setup) Build a workflow named “Demo Workflow” that posts a greeting in #general when triggered
setup_steps: Click the workspace name at the top of the left sidebar.
Click Tools.
Click Workflow Builder.
In the Workflow Builder window, click Create in the upper-right corner.
In the Name field, type Demo Workflow.
Click Next.
Under Select a trigger, click Shortcut.
Click Next.
Click Add step.
Click Send a message.
Open the Channel drop-down and click #general.
Click in the message text box and type Hello from workflow!.
Click Save.
Click Publish in the upper-right corner.
Click Done to close Workflow Builder.
main_task: Trigger the “Demo Workflow” from the shortcut menu
main_steps: Click the lightning bolt icon to the left of the message box at the bottom of Slack.
Type Demo Workflow.
Click Demo Workflow in the list that appears.

setup_task: (Setup) Post the URL allowlist link so it can be opened from Slack
setup_steps: Click the Direct messages section to expand it if it is collapsed.
Click your own name to open a DM with yourself.
Click inside the message field at the bottom of the window.
Type "https://my.slack.com/help/urls".
Press Enter to send the message.
main_task: Open Slack’s allowlist URLs help page
main_steps: Click the link "https://my.slack.com/help/urls" that you just posted.

setup_task: (Setup) Install the Google Calendar app so it appears in the Installed Apps list
setup_steps: Click Apps in the left sidebar.
Click Add apps at the top of the Apps view.
In the search field at the top of the Slack Marketplace window, type Google Calendar.
Press Enter.
Click Google Calendar in the search results.
Click the Add to Slack button.
Click Allow on the permission page to complete the installation.
main_task: Reinstall the Google Calendar app to rotate its token
main_steps: Click Apps in the left sidebar.
Click Add apps.
Click Manage in the upper-right corner of the Slack Marketplace window.
Click Installed Apps in the left panel.
In the search box, type Google Calendar.
Click Google Calendar in the results.
Click the Configuration tab on the app page.
Scroll to the bottom and click Remove App.
Click Remove App in the confirmation dialog.
Wait until the Install button appears, then click Install.
Click Allow on the permission page to finish reinstalling the app.

main_task: Install the “Zoom” calling app from the Slack Marketplace
main_steps: Click the “Apps” icon in the left sidebar.
Click “Add apps”.
Click the search field at the top of the App Directory window.
Type Zoom and press Enter.
Click the app labeled “Zoom”.
Click the “Add to Slack” or “Install” button.
Click “Add” to confirm.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a Salesforce-linked Slack channel named “salesforce-deal-update”
setup_steps: Click the + icon next to Channels in the left sidebar.
Click Create a channel.
In the Name field, type salesforce-deal-update.
Click the Public option.
Click Create.
If an Add people window appears, click Skip for now.
main_task: Post an update message in the “salesforce-deal-update” channel so it syncs with the connected Salesforce record
main_steps: Click the salesforce-deal-update channel in the left sidebar.
Click inside the message field at the bottom of the window.
Type Budget updated to $500k.
Press Enter.

main_task: Restrict the use of @channel and @here mentions to Workspace Owners only
main_steps: Click Admin in the left sidebar.
Click Workspace settings in the menu that appears.
Click Roles & permissions.
On the Account types page, locate the row labeled “Use @channel and @here in channels”.
Click the three dots icon at the end of that row.
Click Edit permission.
In the permission dropdown, click Workspace Owners only.
Click Save.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a new public channel named “announcements-test”
setup_steps: Click the plus (+) button next to “Channels” in the left sidebar.
Click “Create a channel”.
In the Channel name field, type announcements-test.
Click “Create”.
If an invite dialog appears, click “Skip for now”.
main_task: Restrict posting in “announcements-test” so only owners and admins can post messages
main_steps: Click the channel “announcements-test” in the sidebar.
Click the channel name “announcements-test” at the top of the conversation header.
In the channel details pane, click the “Settings” tab.
Next to “Posting permissions”, click “Edit”.
Select the option “Only owners and admins can post”.
Click “Save Changes”.

main_task: Create a custom display name guideline policy that requires members to use their full legal first and last name
main_steps: Click the organization name in the sidebar.
Click Tools & settings.
Click Organization settings.
In the left column, click Settings.
Click Organization Policies.
Click Display name guidelines.
Click Add policy.
Click the radio button labeled Custom Guidelines.
Type All members must use their full legal first and last name.
Click Save Policy.
Click Create Policy to confirm.

main_task: Disallow message editing for all members in the organization
main_steps: Click the organization name in the left sidebar.
Click Tools & settings in the menu that appears.
Click Organization settings.
In the left sidebar, click Settings.
Select Organization Policies.
Click the Permissions tab.
Next to Message Editing, click Add Policy or Edit.
Select Never in the options for when members can edit messages.
Click Save Policy.

main_task: Restrict channel posting permission changes to Workspace Owners only
main_steps: Click Admin in the left sidebar.
Click Workspace settings in the menu.
Click Roles & permissions.
On the Account types page, click the three dots icon next to Edit channel posting permissions.
Click Edit permission.
Select Workspace Owners from the list of roles.
Click Save.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a new channel to use for generating an email address
setup_steps: Click the + icon next to Channels in the left sidebar.
Click “Create a channel”.
In the Name field, type “project-email”.
Click “Create”.
main_task: Generate an email address for the #project-email channel
main_steps: Click the “#project-email” channel in the sidebar.
Click the channel name in the header to open Channel details.
Click the “Integrations” tab in the Channel details pane.
Next to Email, click “Create email address”.
In the confirmation window, click “Create email address” again.
Wait until the unique email address appears on the screen.

main_task: Set “Zoom” as the default third-party calling app in Slack
main_steps: Click your workspace name in the top-left corner of the Slack window.
Click Preferences in the drop-down menu.
Click Advanced in the left sidebar of the Preferences window.
In the Calling section, click the drop-down menu next to “When placing calls, use”.
Click Zoom from the list of options.
Press Esc to close the Preferences window.

setup_task: (Setup) Draft a stand-up reminder message
setup_steps: Click the “general” channel in the left sidebar.
Click inside the message field at the bottom of the channel.
Type “Daily stand-up will start in 10 minutes.”
main_task: Notify the entire channel by adding an @channel mention and sending the message
main_steps: Click at the beginning of the draft message in the message field.
Type “@channel ”.
Press Enter to send the message.

main_task: Change the workspace message retention setting to delete messages older than 90 days
main_steps: Click the workspace name at the top of the left sidebar.
Click "Tools & settings" in the menu that appears.
Click "Workspace settings".
Next to "Data retention", click "Expand".
Click the message retention drop-down menu.
Select "Delete messages older than 90 days".
Click "Save".
In the confirmation window, click "Save" again.

setup_task: (Setup) Populate the Start date profile field with a value
setup_steps: Click the workspace name in the top-left corner of the Slack window.
Click View profile.
Click Edit profile.
Click the Start date field.
Type January 15, 2018.
Click Save changes.
main_task: Enable profile celebrations for the Start date field
main_steps: Click Admin in the left sidebar.
Click Workspace settings from the menu that opens.
Click Profiles.
Below About me, click Edit to the right of Start date.
Click the toggle next to Celebration events to turn it on.
Click Publish Changes.

setup_task: (Setup) Create a thread to later manage its notifications
setup_steps: Click inside the message field at the bottom of the default #general channel.
Type "Hello team" and press Enter.
Hover over the message you just sent and click the "Reply in thread" speech-bubble icon.
In the thread pane on the right, click the reply field, type "First reply" and press Enter.
main_task: Turn off notifications for replies in the created thread
main_steps: Hover over the original "Hello team" message in the channel.
Click the three dots "More actions" icon that appears.
Select "Turn off notifications for replies" from the menu.

setup_task: (Setup) Insert a date into a new canvas for testing reminder creation
setup_steps: Click the plus (+) icon next to “Canvas” in the left sidebar.
Click “New canvas”.
Type “December 31st” in the blank canvas.
Press Enter.
main_task: Add a custom 3:00 PM reminder to the “December 31st” date in the canvas
main_steps: Click the text “December 31st” to highlight the recognized date.
Hover the mouse pointer over the highlighted date.
Click the Add reminder (bell) icon that appears above the date.
Click “Custom time”.
Type 3:00 in the time field.
Select “PM” if needed.
Click “Set reminder”.

main_task: Open the Slack Support contact form to request a message retention override policy
main_steps: Click the question-mark Help icon in the top-right corner of the Slack window.
In the Help menu that appears, click “Contact Us”.
Wait for the Slack Support contact form to open in a new browser tab or window.

main_task: Send a message to notify only active members in #general using @here
main_steps: Click the “#general” channel in the left sidebar.
Click inside the message input field at the bottom.
Type “@here Hello team, meeting starts in 5 minutes.”
Press Enter.

main_task: Add an emoji alias named ":goodjob:" for the existing 👍 (thumbsup) emoji and send a message with it
main_steps: Click the #general channel in the left sidebar.
Click the smiley face emoji icon at the right side of the message field to open the emoji picker.
Click the "Add Emoji" button at the bottom of the picker.
Click the "Alias" tab at the top of the Add Emoji window.
Click the "Choose emoji" field, type "thumbsup", and select the 👍 emoji from the results.
Click the "Enter alias" field and type "goodjob" (without colons).
Click the "Save" button.
In the message field, type ":goodjob:".
Press Enter to send the message and show the 👍 emoji in the channel.

main_task: Enable canvas version history and allow restoration for the workspace
main_steps: Click Admin in the left sidebar.
Click Workspace settings in the menu that appears.
Scroll to the Canvases section and click Expand next to it.
Click the checkbox labeled Show canvas version history and allow restoration to add a checkmark.
Click Save.

main_task: Set the workspace’s message editing permission to “Never”
main_steps: Click Admin in the left sidebar.
Select Workspace settings from the dropdown menu.
Click the Permissions tab at the top of the settings window.
Locate Message Editing and click the Expand button next to it.
Open the drop-down menu under ‘Allow members to edit messages’.
Click Never in the list.
Click Save at the bottom of the section.

setup_task: (Setup) Post a sample message to start a thread
setup_steps: Click the #general channel in the left sidebar.
Click the message input field at the bottom of the channel view.
Type "Project update is scheduled for tomorrow."
Press Enter to send the message.
main_task: Reply to the posted message in a thread and send the reply back to the channel
main_steps: Hover the mouse over the message "Project update is scheduled for tomorrow."
Click the Reply in thread icon that appears.
Click the thread reply input field on the right side.
Type "Looking forward to the details."
Click the checkbox labeled Also send to #general (or Send to channel).
Press Enter to send the reply.

main_task: Create an app approval rule that sends internal app requests for review
main_steps: Click the workspace name in the top-left corner of Slack.
Click "Settings & administration".
Click "Manage apps".
In the left sidebar, click "App Approvals".
Click the "Create rule" button.
Open the first dropdown that starts with "If app requested is".
Select "Internal app" from the list.
Open the action dropdown that starts with "then".
Select "Send for review".
Click "Create" (or "Save") to add the rule.

main_task: Promote a workspace member from Regular Member to Workspace Admin
main_steps: Click your organization name in the Slack sidebar.
Click Tools & settings in the menu.
Click Manage members.
If a workspace list appears, click the workspace you want to manage.
Locate the first member listed under your own name in the Members table.
Click the three dots icon on the right of that member’s row.
Click Change account type.
Select Workspace Admin.
Click Save.

main_task: Disable two-factor authentication for the first member in the workspace list
main_steps: Click the workspace name in the sidebar.
Hover over Tools & settings.
Click Manage members.
Click the three dots icon to the right of the first member in the list.
Click Disable two-factor authentication.
In the confirmation dialog, click Disable.

main_task: Install the Google Authenticator app from the Google Play Store as recommended for Android
main_steps: Tap the Play Store icon on the home screen.
Tap the search bar at the top.
Type "Google Authenticator" and press the search key.
Tap the app titled "Google Authenticator" by Google LLC in the search results.
Tap the "Install" button.
Wait until the download finishes and the "Open" button appears.

setup_task: (Setup) Add a sample domain to prepare for verification
setup_steps: Click Apps in the left sidebar.
Type OneDrive and SharePoint into the search field.
Click the OneDrive and SharePoint app from the results.
Click Add to Slack.
When the app window opens, click the Home tab if it is not already selected.
Click Admin Settings.
Click Add Domain.
Type example.com in the domain field.
Click Add to save the domain.
main_task: Verify ownership of the “example.com” domain
main_steps: In the OneDrive and SharePoint window, stay on the Home tab and click Admin Settings again if needed.
Find the row containing example.com.
Click the verification URL shown under the domain.
On the Microsoft permissions page, click the checkbox confirming Slack’s access to members’ OneDrive and SharePoint accounts.
Click Accept.
Click Open Slack.
Observe that the domain status next to example.com now shows Verified.

setup_task: (Setup) Add a Salesforce channel configuration for the Opportunity record type with the default privacy set to Public
setup_steps: Click Admin in the Slack sidebar.
Click Manage Salesforce Organizations.
Click to select the desired Salesforce org in the list.
Click the Channel configurations tab.
Click the New configuration button.
Open the Record type drop-down and click Opportunity.
Make sure Channel privacy shows Public.
Click Save.
main_task: Change the default privacy of the Opportunity Salesforce channel configuration from Public to Private
main_steps: In the Channel configurations tab, find the row for the Opportunity record type.
Click the three dots icon on the right side of that row.
Click Edit default preferences.
Click the Channel privacy drop-down.
Select Private.
Click Save.

main_task: Restrict the permission to create public channels to Workspace Owners only
main_steps: Click the workspace name at the top of the left sidebar.
Hover the pointer over "Tools & settings".
Click "Workspace settings" from the menu that appears.
If a workspace selection box opens, click the current workspace name to proceed.
In the left sidebar under Administration, click "Manage permissions".
Click "Account Types" near the top of the permissions page.
Locate the row labeled "Create public channels" and click the three-dots icon at the right end of that row.
Click "Edit permission" in the drop-down menu.
Select the radio button "Workspace Owners only".
Click "Save".

main_task: Create a rule that automatically approves internal apps
main_steps: Click the workspace name in the top-left corner of Slack.
Click Settings & administration.
Click Manage apps.
In the Apps Management window, click the Request rules tab.
Click New rule.
Open the Component menu and select App distribution.
Open the Condition menu and select Is.
Open the Comparison menu and select Internal app.
Open the Resolution menu and select Approve.
Click Save.

main_task: Change the default privacy of a Salesforce channel configuration to Limited access for Record owners only
main_steps: Click Admin in the Slack sidebar.
Click Manage Salesforce Organizations.
Click a Salesforce org in the list.
Click the Channel configurations tab.
Click the three dots icon on the right side of an existing Salesforce channel configuration.
Click Edit default preferences.
Under Channel privacy, click the drop-down and select Limited access.
Click the drop-down that appears for permission level and select Record owners.
Click Save.

setup_task: (Setup) Post a message that contains a link preview
setup_steps: Click the channel named “#general” in the sidebar.
Click the message input field at the bottom.
Type “https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ”.
Press Enter to send the message.
Wait until the link preview (unfurl) appears below the sent message.
main_task: Remove the link preview from the posted message
main_steps: Move the mouse cursor over the visible link preview.
Click the x icon that appears on the left side of the preview.

main_task: Enable mandatory two-factor authentication for all workspace members and restrict it to authenticator apps only
main_steps: Click Admin in the left sidebar.
Click Workspace settings.
Click Security in the settings window.
Click Edit next to Two-factor authentication for email sign-in.
Click the checkbox labeled Require members to have 2FA set up.
Click the option Authenticator apps only.
Click Save.

main_task: Allow Multi-Channel Guests to delete their own messages
main_steps: Click Admin in the left sidebar.
Click Workspace settings in the menu that appears.
In the left sidebar, click Roles & Permissions.
Locate the Delete own messages permission, then click the three dots icon to its right.
Click Edit permission.
Check the box for Multi-Channel Guests.
Click Save.
